title: GH#18998: fix review-followup scanner to skip empty bot reviews
body:
## Summary

Fixes two related issues that create noise in the review-followup pipeline:

1. **Empty-review guard** (`quality-feedback-findings-lib.sh`): the scanner fires on PRs where bots post "no feedback" summaries with zero actionable inline comments, creating false-positive quality-debt issues (incident: GH#18834).

2. **raw-sandbox-output over-suppression** (`pulse-ancillary-dispatch.sh`): a triage worker's valid `## Review: Decline` header was suppressed as `raw-sandbox-output` because surrounding log lines confused the sed extraction, preventing the closing comment from being posted.

## Changes

### Fix 1 — PR-level empty-review guard in `_scan_single_pr`

Adds a check AFTER computing `inline_counts_json`: if total inline comment count across all reviewers is 0 **and** every review body matches a negative-finding regex (`no feedback|no review comments|no issues found|lgtm|looks good to me|nothing to flag|...`), return `[]` immediately with a `skip: empty-review PR#N` log line.

- Bypassed when `--include-positive` is set (debugging mode)
- Belt-and-suspenders: the existing per-reviewer `summary_only` filter still runs; this guard catches the case where `state=APPROVED` (not `COMMENTED`) slips through

### Fix 2 — Tighten `raw-sandbox-output` classification

Before classifying as `raw-sandbox-output` (no `## Review` header + infra markers), check if the first non-empty line of `review_text` is `^## Review:`. If it is, re-extract from that line and post (with the normal post-extraction infra check). This handles encoding quirks (CRLF, BOM, raw-mode output) that prevent the existing sed pattern from matching.

## Testing

- 3 new unit tests in `test-quality-feedback-main-verification.sh`:
  - Gemini APPROVED `"no feedback"` + 0 inline comments → 0 findings (GH#18834 regression)
  - Multiple bots all negative + 0 inline → 0 findings
  - Negative top-level summary + inline comments → guard does **not** fire (no over-suppression)
- All 3 pass; only pre-existing `transient API error` test still fails (unrelated, pre-dated this PR)
- ShellCheck: zero violations on all 3 modified files

Resolves #18998

title: t2099: auto-apply 'good first issue' label to tier:simple issues
body:
## Summary

- Extend `_apply_tier_label_replace` in `issue-sync-helper.sh` so `tier:simple` issues automatically also get GitHub's standard `good first issue` label.
- Only applied on `tier:simple`; never auto-removed on escalation (defers to `_is_protected_label` policy).
- 2 new test assertions cover positive and negative paths.

## Why

`tier:simple` issues are, by definition, prescriptive single-file pattern-follows with verbatim code blocks — the exact shape of a community-friendly first contribution. We already produce this pool mechanically; we just were not labelling it for external discovery. Surfacing via GitHub's standard `good first issue` label exposes them to the built-in community filter and third-party discovery sites (goodfirstissue.dev, up-for-grabs, code-triage).

## Design

- **Only ADD, never auto-remove.** `good first issue` is already in `_is_protected_label` and may reflect deliberate human intent. Removing it on escalation would fight maintainer signal.
- **Ensure-then-add.** Uses the existing `gh_create_label` helper (`--force`, idempotent) so repos that don't yet have the label get it created at first application.
- **Gated on the exact tier string.** `[[ "$new_tier" == "tier:simple" ]]` — standard/thinking escalations are unaffected.

## Tests

`test-issue-sync-tier-extraction.sh` grows from 8 → 10 passing assertions:
- `_apply_tier_label_replace adds 'good first issue' when applying tier:simple` ✓
- `_apply_tier_label_replace does NOT add 'good first issue' on tier:standard` ✓
- All 8 prior assertions still pass.

```text
Tests run:    10
Tests failed: 0
```

## Follow-up

After merge, backfill open `tier:simple` issues across pulse repos with the `good first issue` label so the change applies retroactively.

Resolves #19007

## Summary

Phase 1 of the **t2053** shell helper init consolidation roadmap (parent GH#18735). Docs-only foundation for the 7-phase migration.

### What

- NEW: `.agents/reference/shell-style-guide.md` — canonical Patterns A/B/C with rationale, banned patterns, audit data, and migration checklist

- EDIT: `.agents/prompts/build.txt` — one-line Quality Standards rule enforcing the pattern

### Why

PR #18728 fixed one instance of unguarded color re-assignment colliding with `readonly` in `shared-constants.sh`, which had killed `setup.sh` under `set -Eeuo pipefail` and broke auto-update for 4 days (GH#18702 primary, GH#18693 cascade victim). An audit of `.agents/scripts/` (re-run today) found **18 unguarded plain assignments** and **2 production scripts with unguarded `readonly`** (`sonarcloud-autofix.sh`, `coderabbit-cli.sh`) — every one a latent repeat of the same 4-day outage.

This PR establishes the canonical pattern. Phase 2 (separate PR) will add the `shell-init-pattern-check.sh` CI gate. Phases 3–6 migrate the 20 violating scripts in ≤5-file batches.

### Testing

- markdownlint clean on `shell-style-guide.md`
- No code changes; docs and prompt text only
- Audit data in the style guide verified today via `rg` scan

### Key decisions

- **Parent-task keyword rule (t2046)**: uses `For #18735` / `Ref #18735`, NOT `Resolves`. Parent stays open until all phase children merge.
- **No child issue filed for t2053.1**: this PR IS the Phase 1 deliverable. The parent roadmap tracks Phase 1 through the commit's `Ref #18735`. Phase 2+ will get their own child issues once this lands.
- **Pattern B uses `${VAR+x}` not `${VAR:-}`**: the former distinguishes unset from set-to-empty, which matters for edge cases where a parent has intentionally set an empty string.
- **Framework gap noted**: `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr` hardcodes `Resolves #NNN` and hits the parent-task keyword guard when the target is a parent issue. The helper should auto-detect `parent-task` label and emit `For #NNN` instead. Filing separately as a framework task.

title: t2111: fix(issue-sync): ratchet rule in _apply_tier_label_replace — preserve cascade-escalated tier labels
body:
## Summary

`escalate_issue_tier()` in `worker-lifecycle-common.sh` writes escalated tier labels directly to GitHub but leaves the brief file unchanged. The scheduled `issue-sync` enrichment pass then reads the brief and reverts the escalation via `_apply_tier_label_replace`, producing a `tier:standard → tier:thinking → tier:standard` flip-flop visible on GH#19038 label event history (00:38:49 escalate, 00:44:15/16 revert, 01:20 dispatch at `tier:standard` again → same failure).

Fix: add a max-rank **ratchet** to `_apply_tier_label_replace`. Compute the max rank among existing `tier:*` labels using `thinking(2) > standard(1) > simple(0)`. If the existing max outranks the incoming tier, no-op with an info log. Otherwise proceed with the existing replace-all logic. Semantic: brief is a floor, cascade is a ceiling, ceiling wins.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper.sh`
  - Added `_tier_rank` helper (case-statement, O(1)) with a cross-reference comment pointing at the canonical `ISSUE_TIER_LABEL_RANK` in `shared-constants.sh`.
  - Added a ratchet guard inside `_apply_tier_label_replace` that iterates the currently-applied `tier:*` labels, computes the max rank, and returns early with `print_info` when the existing max exceeds the incoming rank.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-tier-label-ratchet.sh` (new, 23 tests)
  - 6 `_tier_rank` unit tests (simple/standard/thinking/empty/unknown/non-tier).
  - 7 ratchet-preservation tests including the exact #19038 flip-flop case (`existing=tier:thinking, incoming=tier:standard → no-op`) and multi-tier collisions.
  - 7 pre-existing-behaviour regression tests (upgrades, bootstrap, idempotent equal) that must not regress.

## Runtime Testing

Risk: **Low** — local shell helper covered by a dedicated test harness; no network, no filesystem side effects outside stubbed `gh`. Self-assessed.

Verification:

```text
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-tier-label-ratchet.sh         → 23/23 pass
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-tier-label-dedup.sh           → 13/13 pass (regression)
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-sync-tier-extraction.sh → 8/8 pass  (regression — includes its own _apply_tier_label_replace assertions, unchanged semantics)
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-label-invariants.sh           → 19/19 pass (regression — reconciler uses same thinking > standard > simple ordering)
shellcheck .agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper.sh               → exit 0 (pre-existing SC1091/SC2016 info-level only)
```

End-to-end proof: patched function run against a stubbed `tier:thinking` issue with a `tier:standard` brief produces zero `gh issue edit` API calls — the trace file is empty, ratchet holds.

## Design Decisions

- **Local `_tier_rank` vs indexing `ISSUE_TIER_LABEL_RANK` from shared-constants:** chose local. The shared array orders `thinking=0` (rank order as position), which would invert the numeric comparison needed here, and a case statement is O(1) without array iteration. Added a comment cross-reference so the relationship is explicit.
- **Ratchet vs write-back to brief:** chose ratchet. Writing escalated tiers back to the brief file would require a commit-per-escalation path, race with concurrent edits, and add cross-file coordination. The ratchet is local to one function, deterministic, and matches the existing max-tier-wins semantics already implemented by `_resolve_worker_tier` (pulse-dispatch-core.sh) and `_first_tier_in_rank_order` (pulse-issue-reconcile.sh).
- **Multi-tier collision handling:** when the issue somehow has both e.g. `tier:simple` and `tier:thinking` AND the incoming is `tier:standard`, the ratchet no-ops entirely (max rank 2 > incoming 1). This is a rare degenerate state; the pulse-issue-reconcile.sh invariant reconciler separately ensures only one tier label per issue, so the collision is transient and the ratchet's "preserve max" behaviour matches the reconciler's own pick.

## Evidence of the Bug

`#19038` label event timeline (via `gh api events`):

```text
00:38:49  marcusquinn           -tier:standard  +tier:thinking   (escalate_issue_tier fires)
00:44:15  github-actions[bot]   -tier:thinking
00:44:16  github-actions[bot]   +tier:standard                   (_apply_tier_label_replace reverts)
01:20:20  pulse dispatches tier:standard again → same worker_failed
```

## Related

- Observed on #19038 (t2103)
- Original `_apply_tier_label_replace`: #18545 (t2012)
- Cascade escalation path: `worker-lifecycle-common.sh:814` `escalate_issue_tier()`
- Tier rank precedent: `pulse-dispatch-core.sh` `_resolve_worker_tier`, `pulse-issue-reconcile.sh` `_first_tier_in_rank_order`

Resolves #19070

title: GH#19044: fix(pulse): resolve FD exhaustion causing merge pass cycles to never complete
body:
## Summary

## Root cause

The launchd plist for the supervisor pulse inherited the macOS default soft FD limit of 256. The pulse sources ~20 modules and spawns gh/jq/git subprocesses across multiple repos per cycle — 256 FDs is structurally insufficient. Additionally, `_simplification_state_refresh()` used process substitution (`< <(jq ...)`) inside a per-file while loop, which leaks FDs in bash 3.2 (the `/bin/bash` version on macOS).

**Effect**: FD exhaustion (`cannot duplicate fd: Too many open files`) caused stages to fail silently, the progress watchdog then killed the pulse before `deterministic_merge_pass` could run, leaving worker PRs unmerged.

## Changes

1. **pulse-wrapper.sh**: Added `ulimit -n 4096` at startup (before sourcing modules) to raise the soft FD limit from 256 to 4096. Added a regression guard that warns if the limit is below 1024.

2. **pulse-simplification-state.sh**: Replaced process substitution (`< <(jq ...)`) with command substitution + here-string (`$(...) <<<`) in `_simplification_state_refresh()` and `_simplification_state_backfill_closed()` to eliminate FD leaks in bash 3.2.

3. **setup-modules/schedulers.sh**: Added `SoftResourceLimits.NumberOfFiles=4096` to the launchd plist generation as defence-in-depth.

## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/pulse-simplification-state.sh,.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh,setup-modules/schedulers.sh

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Low (agent prompts / infrastructure scripts)
- **Verification:** - ShellCheck: all 3 modified files pass clean
- test-pulse-wrapper-characterization.sh: 26/26 pass
- test-simplification-spurious-sweep.sh: 10/10 pass
- test-pulse-wrapper-canary.sh: pass

Resolves #19044

title: t2112+t2113+t2114: self-healing wrapper enforcement — pulse reconcile + CI gate + sub-issue body backfill
body:
## Summary

Closes the framework gap where GitHub issues created by bare `gh issue create` calls (outside the `gh_create_issue` wrapper) stay permanently unblessed — invisible to label reconciliation, dispatch-dedup, and parent-child linking. Moves the "Origin labelling (MANDATORY)" rule in `prompts/build.txt` from **advisory** to **systemic**, and adds a **self-healing** reconcile pass to the pulse so existing unblessed issues are backfilled automatically.

Investigation started from `<webapp>/<webapp>#2395..#2400` — six child issues with aidevops-shaped bodies (`Brief:` + `## Files` + `## Verification`) but zero labels, created by an AI session that composed `gh issue create` calls manually instead of using the wrapper. An in-tree audit found four more framework-internal offenders.

Three cohesive parts in one PR (separate commits, three issues):

### t2114 — `issue-sync-helper.sh backfill-sub-issues` subcommand (commit 1)

Resolves #19093. Works purely from GitHub state — no `TODO.md` or brief file required. Detects parent references via:

1. Dot-notation in title — `^(tNNN)\.N: ` → parent `tNNN`.
2. `Parent: tNNN` / `Parent: #NNN` body line.
3. `Blocked by: tNNN` where the referenced issue carries the `parent-task` label on GitHub.

Resolves both to node IDs and calls the existing `_gh_add_sub_issue` mutation (idempotent). Supports `--dry-run` and `--issue N` (single-issue backfill).

Closes the gap left by GH#18735: `cmd_relationships` is TODO-driven, `_gh_auto_link_sub_issue` is wrapper-driven, and neither handles issues that already exist on GitHub with no TODO entry. Also invoked by t2112 as the sub-issue wiring step.

### t2112 — pulse reconcile pass for labelless aidevops-shaped issues (commit 2)

Resolves #19091. New function `reconcile_labelless_aidevops_issues` in `pulse-issue-reconcile.sh`, wired into `_preflight_ownership_reconcile` in `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh` (runs once per pulse cycle alongside the existing reconcile passes).

Per-repo: scans up to 50 open issues, filters to those whose titles match `^tNNN(\.NNN)*: ` or `^GH#NNN: ` AND have zero labels in `origin:*`, `tier:*`, `status:*` namespaces. Cap: 10 per repo per cycle. For each candidate:

1. Adds `origin:worker` + `tier:standard` as conservative defaults (labelless almost always signals automation bypass).
2. Extracts hashtag labels from the body via regex (letter-led, 2+ chars, excludes `#1234` issue refs) and applies them.
3. Ensures every label exists via `gh label create --force` before the atomic `gh issue edit --add-label …` call.
4. Calls `issue-sync-helper.sh backfill-sub-issues --repo SLUG --issue N` (the t2114 command) to wire parent-child sub-issue links from body parsing.
5. Posts exactly one mentorship comment guarded by the HTML sentinel marker `<!-- aidevops:labelless-backfill -->`. Idempotent across pulse cycles.

### t2113 — systemic `gh_create_issue` / `gh_create_pr` wrapper enforcement (commit 3)

Resolves #19092. Two enforcement points:

- **CI workflow** `.github/workflows/gh-wrapper-guard.yml` — runs on PRs touching `.agents/scripts/**.sh` or `.agents/hooks/**.sh`, invokes `gh-wrapper-guard.sh check --base <base_sha> --head <head_sha>`, fails on violations with a PR comment listing offending lines + fix instructions + allowlist marker.
- **Local pre-push hook** `.agents/hooks/gh-wrapper-guard-pre-push.sh` + dedicated installer `install-gh-wrapper-guard.sh`. If `install-privacy-guard.sh` has already installed a pre-push hook, the installer upgrades it to a **chain dispatcher** that runs both guards in sequence using stdin buffering.

New helper `gh-wrapper-guard.sh` supports three subcommands: `check --base REF --head REF` (diff-scoped for CI and pre-push), `check-staged` (pre-commit), `check-full` (whole-tree audit). Regex requires a command-context leader before `gh` (whitespace, `(`, `=`, `|`, `&`, `;`) so string-literal contexts (`"... gh issue create ..."`) and heredoc text are heuristically excluded. Line-level allowlist: append `# aidevops-allow: raw-gh-wrapper` for audited exceptions.

Bypass: `GH_WRAPPER_GUARD_DISABLE=1` or `git push --no-verify`.

## Test coverage

Three new harnesses (all green):

- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-backfill-sub-issues.sh` — 4 detection methods + dry-run + single-issue mode, stubbed `gh` via bash-function override (the helper prepends `/usr/local/bin` to PATH on source which shadows a PATH-based stub).
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-labelless-reconcile.sh` — 3 fixture issues: labelless aidevops-shaped (processed), non-aidevops (ignored), already-blessed (ignored); body-hashtag extraction for `#ai` and `#security`.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-wrapper-guard.sh` — 9 assertions: clean wrapper use, raw issue/pr create, allowlisted raw call, excluded `shared-constants.sh`, excluded `tests/` fixture, log_info guidance strings (flagged without marker, passed with marker), docs/ path out of scope, `check-full` mini-tree.

## Baseline cleanup

Added `# aidevops-allow: raw-gh-wrapper` markers to seven pre-existing false-positive string-literal cases (`claim-task-id.sh:872`, six lines in `skill-update-helper.sh`). Four remaining genuine in-tree offenders (`full-loop-helper.sh:805`, `pulse-dispatch-large-file-gate.sh:332`, `pulse-triage.sh:720`, `routine-log-helper.sh:896`) are NOT blocked by this PR — the CI gate scans only added/modified lines, not the whole tree. Will be filed as a follow-up migration task.

## Resolves

- Resolves #19092
- Resolves #19093

title: t2115: enforce signature footer in gh_create_issue and gh_create_pr wrappers
body:
## Summary

Signature footers were missing from recent issues and PRs because the `gh_create_issue` / `gh_create_pr` wrappers only enforced origin labels — each caller had to independently call `gh-signature-helper.sh footer` and append the result. This opt-in pattern was frequently missed.

## Root Cause

Three failure modes:
1. **Wrapper gap**: `gh_create_issue()` and `gh_create_pr()` in `shared-constants.sh` only added `--label origin:*` but never appended signature footers
2. **Raw `gh` calls**: Scripts like `pulse-triage.sh`, `pulse-dispatch-large-file-gate.sh`, `routine-log-helper.sh` called `gh issue create` directly, bypassing both wrappers and signatures
3. **Full-loop raw PR creation**: `full-loop-helper.sh` used raw `gh pr create` instead of the wrapper

## Fix

- Added `_gh_wrapper_auto_sig()` in `shared-constants.sh` — extracts `--body`/`--body-file` from args, checks for existing `<!-- aidevops:sig -->` marker, and appends via `gh-signature-helper.sh footer` when missing. Integrated into both `gh_create_issue()` and `gh_create_pr()`.
- Converted raw `gh issue create` / `gh pr create` calls to use the wrappers in 4 scripts.
- New test: `test-gh-wrapper-auto-sig.sh` (15 assertions covering `--body`, `--body=`, `--body-file`, dedup, and arg preservation).

## Files Changed

title: t2116: fix(pulse-merge): update-branch + NMR skip before CONFLICTING-close
body:
Resolves #19106

## Root cause

Over the last 48h of `marcusquinn/aidevops`, **10 of 17 closed-unmerged PRs (~59%) were auto-closed by `pulse-merge.sh`** with `merge conflicts with the base branch` — despite the workers having solved the tasks correctly (all CI green, all tests passing). They sat waiting for a merge cycle while `main` advanced (e.g. ratchet PRs on `complexity-thresholds.conf`, sibling simplifications on `brief/templates.md`), their `mergeable` field flipped to `CONFLICTING`, and `_close_conflicting_pr` immediately closed them. Re-dispatch from scratch → same race → same close → perpetual loop on contended files.

Concrete cases in that window: #19094, #19083, #18988, #18921, #18818, #18944, #18946, #19018.

## Two pathologies fixed

### 1. Skip CONFLICTING-close for `needs-maintainer-review` PRs

`_process_single_ready_pr` previously checked `mergeable=CONFLICTING` at line 925 **before** the maintainer gate at line 947. A PR parked legitimately waiting for maintainer approval was killed the moment `main` advanced — punishing review latency by discarding worker effort. PR #18988 (created 19:25, closed 20:29 after ~1h wait) and #19083 both hit this exactly.

Now: if the linked issue carries `needs-maintainer-review`, the CONFLICTING-close path is skipped entirely and a one-time rebase nudge is posted (same shape as the existing `origin:interactive` skip).

### 2. Attempt `gh pr update-branch` before closing

Most observed conflicts are purely base-branch advancement on an adjacent file — GitHub's server-side merger can fast-forward `main` into the branch for free. When that succeeds, `mergeable` is re-fetched and the PR continues through the normal merge path in the **same cycle**. Only true semantic conflicts (update-branch returns non-zero) fall through to the close path.

## Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh` — new `_attempt_pr_update_branch` helper and reworked CONFLICTING handling in `_process_single_ready_pr`. ~90 lines added, zero lines removed from existing close logic (defensive: the close path is still there for true conflicts).
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-update-branch.sh` — 5 new tests covering update-branch success/failure, log-tag audit, NMR guard structural verification, and the mergeable-refetch requirement.

## Verification

- All 6 pulse-merge test suites pass: 45 tests total, 0 failures.
- `shellcheck`: zero violations on both modified/added files.
- `bash -n`: syntax clean.

## Follow-ups (separate issues, not blocking this PR)

- Dispatch throttle on overlapping file footprints — prevent parallel CONFLICTING cascades at the source.
- Carry forward the closed PR's diff as worker guidance on the linked issue so the re-dispatched worker starts from work-in-progress rather than from scratch.

title: t2118: carry forward closed-CONFLICTING PR diff to linked issue
body:
## Summary

When `_close_conflicting_pr` closes a worker PR via the "work NOT on main" path, the solved diff was silently discarded. The next worker would re-derive the same solution, hit the same conflict, and the loop would repeat — burning tokens on redundant work.

This PR breaks that loop by carrying the PR diff forward to the linked issue body, giving the next worker a concrete starting point.

## Changes

- **`_carry_forward_pr_diff()` helper** added to `pulse-merge.sh` (new function after `_close_conflicting_pr`):
  - Fetches `gh pr diff` for the closed PR
  - Size-caps at 20KB with truncation note
  - Appends under `## Prior worker attempt (PR #NNN, closed CONFLICTING)` in a `<details>` block
  - Idempotency guard: `<!-- t2118:prior-worker-diff:PR<N> -->` marker prevents duplicate appends
  - Fail-open: any gh API failure is logged and the close still proceeds

- **`_close_conflicting_pr`** updated: in the "work NOT on main" else-branch, extract the linked issue and call `_carry_forward_pr_diff` before the `gh pr close` call

- **Regression test** `test-pulse-merge-carry-forward-diff.sh` (5 assertions):
  1. Happy path: diff appears in issue body with marker and section heading
  2. Idempotency: second call for same PR makes no edit
  3. Size cap: 25KB diff truncated with `... (truncated, full diff at PR #N)` note
  4. `origin:interactive` skip: static analysis confirms guard is before carry-forward call
  5. Empty diff: gracefully skipped without issue edit

## Verification

```
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh        # 0 violations
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-carry-forward-diff.sh  # 5/5 pass
grep -c 't2118:prior-worker-diff' .agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh   # 2
```

Resolves #19142

title: GH#19137: fix(dispatch-dedup-cost): broaden token-spend sed pattern for any prefix and time format
body:
## Summary

Addresses review bot feedback from PR #18931: the sed pattern used to normalize token-spend footer strings in `_sum_issue_token_spend` was fragile — it only stripped time infixes for the `spent` prefix and was limited to 1-2 time units (`[0-9]+[dhms]( [0-9]+[mh])?`).

**Change:** Replace the narrow infix-stripping sed pattern with a broader one that:
- Handles both `spent` and `has used` prefixes
- Handles any time format (including days+hours+minutes), using `(.* and )?` to match the optional infix
- Keeps the subsequent `grep -oE '(spent|has used) [0-9,]+ tokens'` extraction intact

**Before:**
```
sed -E 's/(spent )[0-9]+[dhms]( [0-9]+[mh])? and /\1/g'
```

**After:**
```
sed -E 's/(spent|has used) (.* and )?([0-9,]+ tokens)/\1 \3/g'
```

Also updated the inline comment to document the `2d 3h 15m` multi-unit time format example.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-cost.sh` — zero violations
- Logic verified manually against all four documented footer shapes: no-time, minutes, hours+minutes, historical `has used` wording.

title: t2119: feat(worker-reliability): plist drift regen + no_work escalation guard + no_activity output preservation
body:
Resolves #19160

## Summary

Bundled worker reliability self-heal covering three distinct gaps discovered during the t2116 session investigation (session memory `mem_20260415053833`). Each part is separately scoped but tightly coupled to the same symptom — workers dying at ~30s with `result:"no_activity" exit_code:75` — so they ship as one audit-trail-coherent PR.

## Part A — `aidevops update` regenerates drifted launchd plists

**Problem.** PR #19079 (merged 02:08 UTC, 15 Apr) added `SoftResourceLimits: NumberOfFiles: 4096` to `setup-modules/schedulers.sh` to fix FD exhaustion killing pulse workers. The code landed, but the fix stayed **invisible to users for hours** because `auto-update-helper.sh` syncs scripts but never touches `~/Library/LaunchAgents/*.plist`. Users kept hitting the 256-FD launchd default until someone ran `setup.sh --non-interactive` manually. On my own machine the t2116 session exposed this: running setup.sh regenerated the plist, the next pulse cycle raised `maxfiles → 4096`, and the next worker for #19109 went from 30s-no-activity deaths to a 572s productive run that completed successfully.

**Fix.** In `auto-update-helper.sh`, add `check_launchd_plist_drift()` called from `run_freshness_checks`. It hashes `setup-modules/schedulers.sh` and compares against the hash recorded by the last setup.sh run. On mismatch (including the bootstrap case where no hash exists), it re-runs `setup.sh --non-interactive` to regenerate all installed plists. Rate-limited to once per 6 hours so auto-update cycles don't repeatedly re-run setup.

In `setup-modules/schedulers.sh`, add `_schedulers_record_template_hash()` called unconditionally from `setup_supervisor_pulse`. Whole-file hashing is the simplest signal that any plist-generating change has occurred (FD limits, env vars, StartInterval, labels, any LaunchAgent schedulers.sh touches).

Self-healing: existing installs pre-dating t2119 have no stored hash, so the first post-t2119 auto-update cycle treats them as drifted and regenerates the plists automatically. No user action required.

## Part B — Suppress false-positive escalation blocks on infrastructure deaths

**Problem.** `worker-lifecycle-common.sh` `escalate_issue_tier()` posts "Escalation Blocked: Missing Implementation Context" when two consecutive workers fail at the same tier and the issue body lacks `## How` / file paths. During the t2116 investigation I found this gate firing on issues where the workers died in setup (FD exhaustion, plugin init crash, auth refresh race) BEFORE ever reading the brief — wrongly blaming the brief and freezing issues #19037, #19038, #19099, #19110 that had perfectly good content. The gate logic only made sense when the model actually engaged with the content.

**Fix.** `crash_type` is already plumbed through to `escalate_issue_tier`. `"no_work"` specifically means "worker exited during setup without reading target files" — which is exactly the false-positive case. Guard the body-quality gate call with `if [[ "$crash_type" != "no_work" ]]`. For `no_work`, skip the gate entirely and let the normal tier escalation (or no escalation, if already at tier:thinking) proceed.

## Part C — Preserve worker output on `no_activity` for post-mortem diagnostics

**Problem.** `_handle_run_result` unconditionally `rm -f "$output_file"` on the no_activity path. This erases the only forensic evidence of WHY the worker exited without producing any JSON events — opencode stderr via tee, plugin init errors, sandbox exec trace, SQLite migration output, auth refresh messages. The t2116 session had to reproduce failures manually because no preserved artifacts existed. Even after fixing the FD gap, the residual 30s failures I observed on #19114 post-reload couldn't be diagnosed further without real output.

**Fix.** Replace the unconditional delete with `_preserve_no_activity_output` that:
- Moves (not copies — disk-bounded) the output file to `~/.aidevops/logs/worker-no-activity/<ts>-<session>-<model>.log`
- Size-caps at 256 KB with a truncation marker on overflow (interesting content always lands in the first few KB for this failure mode)
- Retention-caps the diagnostic directory to 50 files (bounded even on a looping failure)
- Best-effort throughout — a preservation failure never propagates into the caller's error handling

Operators can now read the actual opencode stderr for every no_activity failure and fix the underlying cause instead of guessing.

## Files changed

- `.agents/scripts/auto-update-helper.sh` — new `check_launchd_plist_drift()` + hook in `run_freshness_checks`
- `setup-modules/schedulers.sh` — new `_schedulers_record_template_hash()` + unconditional call from `setup_supervisor_pulse`
- `.agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-common.sh` — `escalate_issue_tier` skips body-quality gate when `crash_type="no_work"`
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh` — new `_preserve_no_activity_output()` + `_handle_run_result` calls it instead of `rm -f` on the no_activity path
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-reliability-self-heal.sh` — 10 regression tests across all three parts

## Verification

- **10 new regression tests pass** (5 drift + 1 structural escalation + 4 preservation)
- **All 6 existing pulse-merge test suites pass** (51 tests, 0 regressions)
- **shellcheck**: zero violations on the four modified files and the new test file (pre-existing SC1091/SC2016/SC2027 noise in auto-update-helper.sh untouched — those lines are unchanged by this PR)
- **bash -n**: syntax clean on all changed files
- **End-to-end verification pending on merge**: next pulse cycle after this lands should pick up the drift check during `run_freshness_checks` and leave the stamp recorded; future plist-level PRs will auto-deploy within 10 minutes instead of sitting inert for hours

## Why one PR instead of three

All three parts reinforce each other during on-call debugging:
1. Part A closes the gap that kept #19079 inert (the immediate cause of the observed failures)
2. Part B stops the feedback loop from wrongly blaming good briefs while that gap exists
3. Part C gives operators actual evidence the next time the gap re-opens for a different reason

Shipping them separately would mean three PRs against the same observed symptom with overlapping context, and the user explicitly asked for all three "within this session" so the audit trail stays coherent.

title: t2120: fix(opencode-aidevops): populate detailLogPath/detailMaxBytes in quality-hooks ctx
body:
Resolves #19161

## Root cause

`createQualityHooks` in `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks.mjs:208` built the quality-gate context object without `detailLogPath` or `detailMaxBytes` fields:

```js
const ctx = { scriptsDir, logsDir, qualityLogPath };  // ← fields missing
```

But `qualityDetailLog` in `quality-logging.mjs:81` **reads both of those fields**:

```js
function qualityDetailLog(ctx, label, filePath, report) {
  try {
    mkdirSync(ctx.logsDir, { recursive: true });
    rotateLogIfNeeded(ctx.detailLogPath, ctx.detailMaxBytes);  // undefined
    appendFileSync(ctx.detailLogPath, ...);                     // undefined
  } catch (e) {
    console.error(`[aidevops] Quality detail logging failed: ${e.message}`);
  }
}
```

Node throws exactly `"path must be a string or a file descriptor"` when `appendFileSync` receives `undefined`. The catch swallows the throw, but `console.error` still writes the red `[aidevops] Quality detail logging failed: path must be a string or a file descriptor` line to stderr **on every worker file-write that triggers a quality-gate violation**.

Worse: because the `appendFileSync` always failed, real quality-gate diagnostics (shellcheck reports, markdown lint, positional-param validator, secret scan details) were silently lost for every file edit. The framework's own write-time quality discipline was invisible — the detail log it relied on was never written.

## Fix

```diff
 export function createQualityHooks(deps) {
   const { scriptsDir, logsDir } = deps;
   const qualityLogPath = join(logsDir, "quality-hooks.log");
-  const ctx = { scriptsDir, logsDir, qualityLogPath };
+  const detailLogPath = join(logsDir, "quality-hooks-detail.log");
+  const detailMaxBytes = 5 * 1024 * 1024; // 5MB before rotation
+  const ctx = {
+    scriptsDir,
+    logsDir,
+    qualityLogPath,
+    detailLogPath,
+    detailMaxBytes,
+  };
```

Five-line fix for a bug that was silently corrupting every worker session's stderr and defeating the framework's own quality gates.

## Regression test

New `.agents/scripts/tests/test-quality-hooks-ctx.sh` with two assertions:

1. **Structural** — extracts the `createQualityHooks` function body via `awk` and asserts all five required ctx fields (`scriptsDir`, `logsDir`, `qualityLogPath`, `detailLogPath`, `detailMaxBytes`) are present. Prevents future refactors from regressing the fix silently.
2. **Runtime** — spawns Node with a driver script that:
   - Calls `createQualityHooks({ scriptsDir, logsDir })` with a fresh tmp dir
   - Writes a deliberately-violating shell script to trigger `runShellQualityPipeline` → `logQualityGateResult` → `qualityDetailLog`
   - Captures `console.error` output during `hooks.toolExecuteAfter(...)` execution
   - Asserts no throw AND no `"Quality detail logging failed"` line leaked to stderr

Both tests pass locally; shellcheck clean.

## Impact on the open-issues backlog

This bug was a quiet multiplier on worker unreliability. Every headless worker that edited any file produced this red error on stderr, which:

1. **Polluted the output stream** that `output_has_activity` in `headless-runtime-lib.sh:536` parses to detect LLM activity. The parser looks only at JSON-event lines starting with `{`, so plain-text `[aidevops]` error lines are skipped — but they're real bytes written to the worker output file that operators reading logs had to mentally filter out.
2. **Silently disabled the quality-gate detail log** (`~/.aidevops/logs/quality-hooks-detail.log` was never written), so the framework's own write-time shellcheck / markdown lint / secret scan reports were invisible. Any "why didn't shellcheck catch this?" debugging was dead-end.
3. **Didn't directly cause the 30s no_activity deaths** that t2116/t2119 addressed — those are infrastructure (FD exhaustion + plist drift deployment gap). But it was a parallel quality-of-debugging regression that made every other investigation harder.

Combined with the t2119 bundle (plist drift regen + no_work escalation guard + no_activity output preservation) and the t2116 merge-pass fix, the worker reliability surface is now three layers deeper than it was at the start of the session.

## Files changed

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks.mjs` — 5-line ctx fix + comment
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-quality-hooks-ctx.sh` — new 2-assertion regression test

title: t2121: fix(opencode-aidevops): buffer stream chunks by newline in mcp prefix strip
fix(canary): DB isolation + output-aware check + archival paste fix
body:
## Summary

Fixes the root cause of all headless workers failing to launch since the opencode 1.3→1.4.6 upgrade. Workers were being dispatched, creating sessions with 0 tokens, and dying within seconds — burning through tier escalation cycles without doing any work.

**Causal chain:**
1. Session archival broken (macOS `paste -s` doesn't accept pipe input) → 3232 sessions accumulated → DB grew to 3.7GB
2. Canary test opens the 3.7GB shared DB without isolation → startup exceeds 20s timeout → SIGALRM kills process (exit=142)
3. Canary check requires `exit=0 AND CANARY_OK` → discards valid model response because exit≠0
4. All worker dispatches blocked by false canary failure

**Fixes:**
- **Canary DB isolation**: temp `XDG_DATA_HOME` with fresh DB + auth.json copy (same pattern workers use since GH#17549)
- **Output-aware check**: `CANARY_OK in output` is the real health signal, not exit code. Timeout 20s→60s
- **Archival**: `paste -sd,` → `tr '\n' ',' | sed 's/,$//'` for macOS compat

**Verified:** canary passes cleanly with isolation (exit=0, CANARY_OK found). Archival successfully moved 3232 sessions.

Resolves the systemic worker failure pattern visible on #19158, #19154, #19140, #19139, and many others.

title: fix(worker-reliability): relax kill thresholds to let workers complete
body:
## Summary

Workers that previously solved issues in 10-15 min were being killed by the pulse's stale recovery mechanism before completion. Evidence: #19165 worker consumed 66K tokens, was actively editing `pulse-dep-graph.sh`, then stale recovery classified it as `no_work` and killed it at the 15-min mark.

**Root cause:** 9 different mechanisms can kill workers, most with thresholds set too aggressively (15 min stale recovery, 5 min activity watchdog, 10 min progress timeout). The per-worker activity watchdog (output file growth monitoring) is the only mechanism that correctly identifies dead workers — everything else was killing active ones.

**Changes:**
- `PULSE_STALE_THRESHOLD`: 15→60 min
- `PULSE_IDLE_TIMEOUT`: 10→30 min
- `PULSE_IDLE_CPU_THRESHOLD`: 5→2%
- `PULSE_PROGRESS_TIMEOUT`: 10→30 min
- `PULSE_COLD_START_TIMEOUT`: 20→30 min
- `PULSE_UNDERFILLED_STALE_RECOVERY`: 15→60 min
- `STALE_OPENCODE_MAX_AGE`: 4→8h
- Activity watchdog stall: 5→10 min
- Activity watchdog phase1: 30→60s

The activity watchdog remains the real kill mechanism — it monitors output file growth and kills workers whose output stops growing for 10 min (genuinely dead). All pulse-level timeouts now defer to it.

Follow-up to #19166 (canary DB isolation fix).

title: GH#19165: fix(dep-graph): preserve subtask decimal suffix in blocked-by parsing
body:
## Summary

`blocked-by:t325.1` was parsed as blocking on task `t325` (the parent, still open) instead of `t325.1` (the child, already closed). This blocked the entire <webapp> subtask chain (#2395-#2400) from being dispatched despite their actual dependencies being resolved.

**Root cause:** `grep -oE '[0-9]+'` strips everything after the decimal point. Three extraction sites had this pattern — the shell helpers, the jq pipeline in the dep-graph builder, and the title parser.

**Fix:** All three sites now use patterns that preserve the full dotted suffix (`t325.1` → `325.1`).

Resolves #19165

title: fix(nmr): reset stale-recovery tick counter on auto-approve
body:
## Summary

Auto-approve and stale-recovery were fighting each pulse cycle — approve removes NMR, stale-recovery re-adds it because the tick count stays above threshold. This caused 5 issues to be permanently stuck with NMR despite the maintainer being the author.

Fix: when auto-approve removes NMR, post a `stale-recovery-tick:0` reset comment. This gives the issue a fresh dispatch attempt. If the worker fails again, the counter builds back up naturally and NMR gets re-applied legitimately.

The flow is now: NMR applied (worker failed N times) → maintainer/interactive session removes NMR → auto-approve resets tick counter → fresh dispatch attempt → if it fails again, counter rebuilds → NMR re-applied after threshold.

title: fix: use Response.json() in proxy handlers to avoid Bun _Response type mismatch
body:
## Summary

- Replace `new Response(JSON.stringify(...))` with `Response.json()` in both `claude-proxy.mjs` and `google-proxy.mjs` to avoid Bun's cross-realm `_Response` type rejection
- OpenCode's plugin loader rebinds the `Response` constructor to a realm-local `_Response` class; `Bun.serve` then rejects it with `Expected a Response object, but received '_Response'`
- `Response.json()` (Fetch API static method) constructs through Bun's native internal path, bypassing the mismatch
- Falls back to `new Response()` for runtimes without `Response.json()`

For #19175 (tracks the full `_Response` fix family — this PR is the claude/google half; #19181 extends the same pattern to cursor and provider-auth)

## Evidence

Before fix — error spamming every few minutes in `opencode-web.service` journal:
```
error: Expected a Response object, but received '_Response {
  [Symbol(cache)]: [ 200, "{\"object\":\"list\",\"data\":[...]}" ...
}'
```

After fix — 42 min runtime, zero errors, `/v1/models` returns clean JSON.

## Files changed

- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/claude-proxy.mjs` — add `jsonResponse()`/`textResponse()` helpers, replace 5 `new Response()` call sites
- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/google-proxy.mjs` — same pattern, replace 5 `new Response()` call sites

title: t2122: extend Response.json() fix to remaining opencode plugin Bun.serve callers
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #19174 (superdav42 claude+google proxy fix). Extracts the `jsonResponse`/`textResponse` helpers into a shared `response-helpers.mjs` module and routes three untouched `Bun.serve`-backed fetch handlers through it so the realm-boundary workaround has exactly one audited call site for the whole plugin.

Resolves #19175

## Discovered during review

While reviewing #19174 I traced `new Response(JSON.stringify(...))` across the plugin and found seven more call sites that the PR does not touch:

| File | Sites | Has its own `Bun.serve`? | Risk |
|------|-------|--------------------------|------|
| `cursor/proxy.js` | 5 (4 JSON, 1 text/404) | **Yes** (line 160) | **High** — any user enabling the Cursor provider would hit the same `_Response` journal spam on the first `/v1/models` request |
| `cursor/proxy-stream.js` | 1 (SSE streaming) | No (shared with `cursor/proxy.js`) | Low (streaming hasn't been observed to fail) |
| `provider-auth-request.mjs` | 1 (streaming passthrough) | No (wrapper on fetched response) | Low (streaming hasn't been observed to fail) |

`cursor/proxy.js` is the real concern: it has its own `Bun.serve` instance with identical JSON-response idiom. If `#19174`'s root-cause hypothesis is correct, this proxy is a dormant time-bomb.

## Changes

- **NEW:** `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/response-helpers.mjs` — shared module with `jsonResponse(data, init?)` and `textResponse(body, init?)`. `jsonResponse` uses `Response.json()` when available (native Bun fetch path, bypasses the `_Response` mismatch) with a `new Response(JSON.stringify(...))` fallback for older runtimes. `textResponse` is a thin alias over `new Response(...)` — streaming paths have not been observed to fail in practice, and the alias exists so any future workaround lands in one place. Single source of truth for the whole plugin.
- **EDIT:** `cursor/proxy.js` — 5 sites migrated. 4 use `jsonResponse` (No-user-message 400, chat-completion response, error wrap 500, models list), 1 uses `textResponse` (Not Found 404). Adds one `import` line.
- **EDIT:** `cursor/proxy-stream.js` — 1 SSE streaming response routed through `textResponse`.
- **EDIT:** `provider-auth-request.mjs` — 1 streaming passthrough (MCP prefix strip wrapper) routed through `textResponse`.
- **NEW:** `tests/test-opencode-response-helpers.sh` — smoke test (`node --check` on all four modified files + 5 runtime assertions covering `jsonResponse` default/custom-status/round-trip and `textResponse` plain-text/`ReadableStream`).
- **NEW:** `todo/tasks/t2122-brief.md` — task brief.

## Out of scope (deliberate, deferred)

This PR **does not** touch `claude-proxy.mjs` or `google-proxy.mjs`. #19174 introduces its own local copy of `jsonResponse`/`textResponse` in both files. Migrating those to import from the shared module would produce a trivial merge conflict with #19174 and has zero functional benefit — the helpers are identical. After #19174 merges, a separate follow-up PR will delete the two local copies and add the import.

## Why streaming `textResponse` if it has never been observed to fail

`#19174`'s 42-minute clean run shows that streaming paths (`new Response(stream, ...)`) work fine with the realm-boundary bug present. The likely mechanism isn't pure constructor rebinding — it's probably specific to the `JSON.stringify` + `{headers: {"Content-Type": "application/json"}}` init shape. Migrating streaming responses to `textResponse` (which is `new Response(...)` under the hood) is a pure consistency move: it costs nothing, and if we ever do hit the mismatch on a streaming path, we can add a workaround inside `textResponse` and fix every call site in one edit.

## Testing

- `node --check` clean on all four modified JS files.
- `tests/test-opencode-response-helpers.sh` runs 5 runtime assertions and passes locally.
- `shellcheck` clean on the new test script.
- **Real acceptance** is an opencode-web.service journal run — parallel to #19174's 42-minute evidence. I'll verify after merge.

## Rollback

Trivial. Pure additive — no schema, no config, no state. Delete the shared module, revert the four file edits, and the plugin is back to pre-PR state.

title: fix(deploy): auto-restart pulse after agent deployment

## Summary

Bash processes load `source` files at startup only — deploying updated scripts doesn't affect a running pulse. title: t2123: Configurable review gate rate-limit behavior per tool and per repo

## Summary

- Make `PASS_RATE_LIMITED` behavior configurable at three levels: per-tool, per-repo, and global default
- Fix inaccurate code comment claiming bots review post-merge (they don't — CodeRabbit posts "Review failed — The pull request is closed")

## What

When review bots are rate-limited during merge, the gate now checks a configurable behavior setting instead of always passing. Resolution order:

1. **Per-tool** — `repos.json` → `review_gate.tools.<bot>.rate_limit_behavior`
2. **Per-repo default** — `repos.json` → `review_gate.rate_limit_behavior`

```json
{
  "review_gate": {
```

title: GH#19140: fix(dispatch-dedup): replace --limit 1 with --limit 20 + jq local filter in Check 1b and 2
body:
## Summary

- **Correctness fix**: `_has_open_pr_check_open_body_keyword` (Check 1b) and `_has_open_pr_check_merged_keywords` (Check 2) used `--limit 1` on `gh pr list`. If GitHub's full-text search returned a false-positive PR first, the real matching PR was silently missed — dispatch dedup would allow duplicate dispatch even when an open/merged PR already closed the issue.
- **Approach**: Fetch up to 20 candidate PRs in a single `gh pr list` request with the simpler `"#NNN in:body"` query, then filter locally using `jq` with the closing-keyword regex. This mirrors the pattern already used by Check 1 (`_has_open_pr_check_open_commits`) and was suggested by gemini-code-assist on PR #18915.
- **Tests fixed**: Updated 7 test fixtures in `test-dispatch-dedup-helper-has-open-pr.sh` to use the new `"#NNN in:body"` query key format and include `body` in the `gh pr list` JSON payload (eliminating separate `gh pr view` fixtures for Checks 1b, 2, and 3). The tests were already broken (3 of 10 failing) due to the prior compound keyword query not matching the expected fixture keys.

title: feat(pulse-merge): route CI failures and merge conflicts to issues for worker re-dispatch
body:
## Summary

Closes the feedback loop for worker PRs that fail CI or develop merge conflicts. Previously, these PRs sat blocked indefinitely — the merge pass skipped them, and the linked issue stayed claimed, preventing re-dispatch.

2. **Conflict resolution** (`_dispatch_conflict_fix_worker`): When `update-branch` fails (semantic conflict) on a worker PR, appends a "Merge Conflict Feedback" section with conflicting file list, closes the PR, re-queues the issue. Next worker re-implements on current `main`.

Both use idempotent markers and routing labels. Interactive PRs are always left alone.

body:
## Summary

The `<!-- aidevops-signed-approval -->` marker is trusted by `maintainer-gate.yml` to allow NMR removal. Without locking, a non-collaborator could post a comment containing this marker on a public NMR issue and bypass the gate.

Fix: lock the issue before posting the approval marker. The lock persists through dispatch (t1934 `lock_issue_for_worker`) and unlocks after the worker completes. Only collaborators can comment on locked issues.

title: feat(security): lock maintainer/worker issues at creation to prevent comment injection

Added to both creation paths: `create_github_issue()` in `claim-task-id.sh` and `_push_create_issue()` in `issue-sync-helper.sh`. Only locks owner or `origin:worker` issues — external contributor issues stay unlocked for community discussion.

title: GH#19252: fix(pulse): Bash 3.2 heredoc-in-$() breaks pulse dispatch
body:
## Summary

- **Fix**: Replace `$(cat <<EOF ... EOF)` with plain double-quoted string assignment in `reconcile_labelless_aidevops_issues()` — Bash 3.2 parser cannot handle heredocs inside command substitution
- **CI hardening**: Add native `/bin/bash -n` (Bash 3.2) syntax check on macOS CI runner + regex check for the `$(cat <<` pattern in the Bash 3.2 compat job
- **Docs**: Document the heredoc-in-`$()` footgun in `bash-compat.md`

## Root Cause

The launchd supervisor plist hardcodes `/bin/bash` (Bash 3.2) as the interpreter. The `shared-constants.sh` re-exec guard transparently upgrades to Bash 5, but Bash 3.2 emits parse errors during the `source` pass for any file containing `$(cat <<HEREDOC ... HEREDOC)`. This corrupts function definitions below the error point, silently breaking the reconcile functions that the pulse depends on for issue dispatch.

**Introduced in**: `8f6d1e1e1` (feat(t2112), PR #19098, 2026-04-15) — the `reconcile_labelless_aidevops_issues` function used a heredoc inside `$()` for a comment template.

**Impact**: ~18 hours of blocked pulse dispatch. The pulse continued running (commits, GH comments) but reconcile functions were corrupt — no worker dispatch for queued issues.

## CI Gap Analysis

The existing "Bash 3.2 Compatibility" CI job only greps for three known patterns (`\t`/`\n` in strings, `declare -A`, `declare -n`). It runs on `ubuntu-latest` (Bash 5), so there is no actual Bash 3.2 parser validation. This PR adds:

1. **`/bin/bash -n` on macOS runner** (gold standard) — real Bash 3.2 parser check on all shell scripts, catches ALL syntax incompatibilities
2. **Regex check for `$(cat <<`** (defense in depth) — runs on Ubuntu too, gives a clearer error message

## Files

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh:1159-1171` — replace heredoc-in-$() with quoted string
- EDIT: `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml` — add macOS Bash 3.2 syntax step + heredoc regex check
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/bash-compat.md` — document the pattern

## Verification

```bash
# Passes on both Bash 3.2 and 5:
/bin/bash -n .agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh && echo OK
bash -n .agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh && echo OK
```

Resolves #19252

title: t2139: review-bot-gate require positive completion signal in bot_has_real_review
body:
## Summary

Replaces the negative-only filter in `bot_has_real_review()` with a hybrid classifier that requires both an absence of known non-review patterns AND positive evidence the bot's comment has settled (edited or sufficiently old). Defeats CodeRabbit's two-phase placeholder pattern that was causing PRs to merge in 21-76s before Phase 2 reviews completed.

Resolves #19251

## Why

External contributor @robstiles filed #19251 with strong evidence that `bot_has_real_review()` false-positives on CodeRabbit's Phase 1 placeholder comment:

- 7/7 sampled PRs on a managed private repo merged at ~76s — exactly one `REVIEW_BOT_POLL_INTERVAL` after CodeRabbit's Phase 1 placeholder. CodeRabbit then edited each comment with "Review failed — Pull request was closed or merged during review."
- On this repo, PRs #19239 and #19240 merged in 21-23s with "Review skipped" comments that also bypassed the gate.
- Net result: zero CodeRabbit feedback on these PRs; t2093's `CHANGES_REQUESTED` routing was unreachable.

Root cause: `bot_has_real_review()` (line 224-260 pre-fix) classified any comment that didn't match `RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS` as a real review. It had no concept of completion — only the absence of known-bad patterns. Two-phase posting and non-rate-limit notices ("Review failed", "Review skipped") slipped through.

The t2123 work (PR #19186) only addressed the rate-limited branch (lines 398-417) of `do_check`. The false-positive `found_bots` branch was untouched and hit unconditional PASS.

## What Changed

### `.agents/scripts/review-bot-gate-helper.sh`

1. **Renamed `RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS` → `NON_REVIEW_PATTERNS`** for accuracy. Added 4 new patterns: `"Review failed"`, `"Review skipped"`, `"closed or merged during review"`, `"Auto reviews are limited"`. Old name preserved as a backwards-compat alias.
2. **Added `_get_min_edit_lag()` resolver** mirroring `_get_rate_limit_behavior` — resolves per-tool > per-repo > env var > 30s default from the existing `review_gate` schema.
3. **Added `_comment_is_settled()` helper** — returns 0 if a comment was edited (`updated_at >= created_at + min_lag`) or is older than `min_lag` seconds since `created_at`. Conservative pass on missing/unparseable timestamps.
4. **Updated `bot_has_real_review()`** to require BOTH negative-filter pass AND settled check. Changed jq filter to extract `(created_at, updated_at, body)` tuples instead of just bodies.
5. **Renamed `is_rate_limit_comment` → `is_non_review_comment`**, with thin alias preserved.
6. **Added `_classify_bot_state()`** to power `do_list` output. Returns one of: `real-review`, `not-yet` (placeholder), `non-review-only` (rate-limit/failure/skip), `no-comments`.
7. **Updated `do_list`** to print the disambiguated state instead of always saying "rate-limited (no real review)".

### `.agents/scripts/tests/test-review-bot-gate-completion-signal.sh` (new)

16 unit tests covering:

- All 4 new pattern matches + 1 rejection of real review body + 1 backwards-compat alias.
- 6 settled-check edge cases: recent unedited placeholder rejected, old unedited accepted, recent-edit-under-lag rejected, edit-delta-over-lag accepted, missing timestamps conservative pass, unparseable timestamps conservative pass.
- 4 lag resolver tests: per-tool override, per-repo default, global env, unknown repo.

Sources the helper with `main` invocation stripped (sed-trick) so functions are callable in the test shell. Uses a temp `HOME` with a fixture `repos.json`.

### `.agents/AGENTS.md`

Documents the new `min_edit_lag_seconds` field alongside `rate_limit_behavior` in the `review_gate` section, including the resolution order and a combined example.

### TODO + Brief

`TODO.md` adds the t2139 entry with `ref:GH#19251`. `todo/tasks/t2139-brief.md` is the implementation brief used for this session.

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/review-bot-gate-helper.sh \
  .agents/scripts/tests/test-review-bot-gate-completion-signal.sh
# (clean)

bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-review-bot-gate-completion-signal.sh
# Tests run: 16, failed: 0

npx markdownlint-cli2 .agents/AGENTS.md
# Summary: 0 error(s)
```

## Compatibility

- **Default behaviour unchanged for repos without `review_gate.min_edit_lag_seconds` config** — it just inherits the 30s global default. Repos that have no `review_gate` block at all get the same 30s default.
- **`RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS` and `is_rate_limit_comment` aliases preserved** for any external scripts/tests that might reference them.
- **No new dependencies.** Uses existing `jq`, `gh api`, `date` (cross-platform GNU/BSD).
- **`do_request_retry` and `do_batch_retry` unaffected** — they use `bot_has_real_review` and the new stricter classification just means a few PRs that previously appeared "real-reviewed" will now appear "not-yet" or "non-review-only", which the retry logic already handles correctly.

## Trade-offs

- ~30s slower merge for PRs where CodeRabbit posts a real review — intentional, this is what fixes the bug.
- Marginal extra `gh api` data per call (added `created_at`, `updated_at` to the jq selection). Same number of API calls.

## Self-modifying tooling note

This PR modifies `review-bot-gate-helper.sh` itself, which the merge gate uses. The committed version was tested before commit (16/16 tests pass), and shellcheck is clean. The merge pass against this PR will exercise the new code path on its own checks; if a CodeRabbit Phase 1 placeholder lands on this PR, the new gate will correctly hold the merge until Phase 2 settles, demonstrating the fix end-to-end.

title: GH#19296: remove ineffective || return 1 from _generate_seo_commands
body:
## Summary

Removes the `|| return 1` pattern added to `_generate_seo_commands` in PR #19281, which was ineffective and actively masked failures.

## Root Cause

Per the bash spec: when a function is called as `fn || return 1`, `set -e` is suppressed for **all commands within `fn`'s body** — not just the function call itself. Both `_generate_seo_keyword_commands` and `_generate_seo_ai_commands` also end with explicit `return 0`, meaning they always return success regardless of any internal failures (e.g., a failed file write in `write_command`).

The net effect: the `|| return 1` in PR #19281 suppressed `set -euo pipefail` within the sub-functions while providing no compensating propagation. Failures were masked.

## Fix

Call the sub-functions directly and rely on `set -euo pipefail` (line 38) to propagate failures naturally — which is what the code did before PR #19281. This is the correct pattern when the sub-functions themselves use `set -e` semantics rather than explicit error returns.

## Verification

- `shellcheck` passes (no new violations)
- `_generate_seo_commands` now correctly propagates any failure from its sub-functions via `set -e`

Resolves #19296

title: t2141: full-loop-helper merge auto-resolve --admin/--auto mutual exclusion
body:
## Summary

`cmd_merge` in `full-loop-helper.sh` now detects when both `--admin` and `--auto` are passed and resolves in favour of `--admin` (drops `--auto` with an informational message), instead of passing both through to `gh pr merge` and surfacing the opaque CLI error:

```
specify only one of `--auto`, `--disable-auto`, or `--admin`
```

Resolves #19310

## Why

Discovered live during the t2139 merge today (PR #19309): `full-loop-helper.sh merge ... --admin --auto` failed because the wrapper passed both flags through. The error message is unhelpful — there is no English-level signal that "admin override AND auto-merge" is a contradictory combination. They read as compatible compounded intent.

`--admin` already implies "merge now via owner override". `--auto` ("queue and wait for checks") is functionally redundant when `--admin` is set. So the silent-resolve direction is unambiguous.

## What Changed

### `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh:1095-1145`

Added a 5-line conflict-resolution block in `cmd_merge` after the flag-parsing loop:

```bash
if [[ "$has_admin" -eq 1 && "$has_auto" -eq 1 ]]; then
    print_info "Both --admin and --auto were specified; gh pr merge rejects this combination."
    print_info "Resolving in favour of --admin (overrides branch protection now); dropping --auto."
    has_auto=0
fi
```

Also updated:

- `cmd_merge` docstring (lines 1085-1099) — notes the mutual exclusion.
- `show_help` text (lines ~1170) — notes the resolution.

title: GH#19297: fix: propagate write failures through full call chain in generate-claude-commands.sh
body:
## Summary

The `|| return 1` fix in `_generate_seo_commands` (PR #19280) was ineffective because the entire call chain below it always returned 0. Gemini correctly identified this in the review of PR #19280.

**Root cause:** When a function is called in a `||` context (e.g., `_generate_seo_keyword_commands || return 1`), bash disables `set -e` for that call AND all sub-calls. Without explicit `|| return 1` at each layer, write failures are silently masked.

## Changes

- **`write_command`**: Added `|| return 1` to the file redirect operation — write failures now propagate
- **`maybe_write_command`**: Changed `write_command "$cmd_name" "$description" "$body"` to use `|| return 1` — propagates `write_command` exit code
- **`_generate_seo_keyword_commands`**: Added `|| return 1` to each `maybe_write_command` call (4 calls)
- **`_generate_seo_ai_commands`**: Added `|| return 1` to each `maybe_write_command` call (7 calls)

## Verification

- `shellcheck` passes (only pre-existing SC1091 info note, unchanged)
- `bash generate-claude-commands.sh --dry-run` produces 114 commands correctly

title: GH#19300: guard auto-approve log and counter behind edit exit code
body:
## Summary

When `gh issue edit` fails to update labels (race condition, permission error, etc.), the previous code silently treated it as a success via `|| true`, logging an "Auto-approved" entry and incrementing `total_approved`. This produced false approval counts.

## Change

Capture the exit code from `gh issue edit` and make the log message and `total_approved` increment conditional on success (`exit_code == 0`). On failure, log a warning instead so the condition is visible.

**File:** `.agents/scripts/pulse-nmr-approval.sh` around line 468

**Before:**
```bash
gh issue edit "$issue_num" --repo "$slug" \
    --remove-label "needs-maintainer-review" \
    --add-label "auto-dispatch" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
echo "[pulse-wrapper] Auto-approved #${issue_num} ..." >>"$LOGFILE"
total_approved=$((total_approved + 1))
```

**After:**
```bash
gh issue edit "$issue_num" --repo "$slug" \
    --remove-label "needs-maintainer-review" \
    --add-label "auto-dispatch" >/dev/null 2>&1
local edit_exit=$?
if [[ "$edit_exit" -eq 0 ]]; then
    echo "[pulse-wrapper] Auto-approved #${issue_num} ..." >>"$LOGFILE"
    total_approved=$((total_approved + 1))
else
    echo "[pulse-wrapper] Auto-approve label update FAILED for #${issue_num} ..." >>"$LOGFILE"
fi
```

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-nmr-approval.sh` — zero violations
- The comment (approval marker + tick reset) is still posted BEFORE the edit, as required by `maintainer-gate.yml` ordering
- Only the log and counter are now gated on edit success

title: t2140: register claude-opus-4-7 as opt-in model
body:
## Summary

Register Claude Opus 4.7 as a selectable option in the aidevops OpenCode plugin. **No default tier mappings change** — `opus`, `coding`, and all fallback chains continue to route to `claude-opus-4-6`. Users opt in via `custom/configs/model-routing-table.json`.

## Why opt-in only (not the new default)

Three concrete regressions vs 4.6:

- **Long-context retrieval collapse** (MRCR v2 8-needle, Anthropic system card §8.7.2):
  - 256K: 91.9% → 59.2% (−32.7 pts)
  - 1M: 78.3% → 32.2% (−46.1 pts)
  - Unsuitable for full-loop workers, cross-file refactors, whole-repo audits.
- **Tokenizer bloat**: English +58.8%, Python +21.4%, mixed multilingual +22.8% (same paragraph, new tokenizer). At identical per-token pricing = 20-60% effective cost increase on our English-heavy prompts.
- **Stricter literal instruction-following** (Anthropic migration guide): prompts tuned for 4.6's looser interpretation may misbehave. Our 50+ headless dispatch scripts aren't yet audited for literal-mode safety.

## Design decision: 200K context, not 1M

4.7 is registered with a 200K context window in `config-hook.mjs` and `claude-proxy.mjs`, even though the API accepts 1M. The 1M window is functionally broken for retrieval per MRCR — advertising it would route users into a dead zone. The existing `/compact` soft-prompt at 200K+ now does the right thing for 4.7 automatically.

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/config-hook.mjs` — `CLAUDE_MODEL_LIMITS` + both provider name maps

title: fix: pulse merge-pass field shift — tab delimiter collapse blocks all PR merges
body:
## Summary

- **Root cause**: `IFS=$'\t' read -r` in `_process_single_ready_pr()` collapses consecutive tab delimiters when `reviewDecision` is `""` (empty string). jq `//` only triggers on `null`/`false`, not empty strings, so `(.reviewDecision // "NONE")` produces `""` → consecutive tabs → Bash collapses them → `pr_author` gets the PR title → `_is_collaborator_author` rejects every PR as "not a collaborator"
- **Impact**: ALL deterministic PR merges across ALL pulse-enabled repos blocked. PRs accumulate indefinitely.
- **Fix**: Replace tab delimiter with ASCII record separator (`\^^` / `0x1E`), a non-whitespace character that Bash never collapses. Also add jq `if-then-else` for `reviewDecision` to properly handle both `null` and empty string.

## Verification

```bash
# Before (Bash 3.2 or modern — same behavior):
# IFS=$'\t' read → pr_review=[marcusquinn] pr_author=[PR TITLE]

# After:
```

title: t2147: contributor insight pipeline — session-miner upstream issue filing with privacy sanitization
body:
## Summary

- New `contributor-insight-helper.sh` — takes session-miner output and files privacy-sanitized issues upstream for contributor-role repos
- Privacy sanitization layer strips private slugs, local paths, credentials, and emails before any content leaves the contributor's machine
- Integrated into `session-miner-pulse.sh` — runs automatically after the existing feedback loop for contributor-role repos
- 22/22 test assertions covering sanitization, dry-run filing, confidence filtering, and error pattern thresholds

## Context

Companion to PR #19350 (t2145: role guard). That PR gates scanners that re-scrape repo data the maintainer already has. This PR builds the value channel in the opposite direction: contributors surface insights from their own usage sessions that only they can observe — instruction candidates ("always use worktrees!"), recurring error patterns, and workflow friction — sanitized and filed upstream as `contributor-insight` issues.

Note: PR #19355 (`feature/t2147-contributor-insight-pipeline`) implemented the same feature but linked to issue #19352 (already closed for unrelated work). This PR corrects that linkage by resolving the correct issue #19356.

## How it works

1. Session-miner runs locally (same as today) — mines steerage, errors, instruction candidates
2. `file_contributor_insights()` in session-miner-pulse.sh iterates repos.json for contributor-role entries
3. For each, calls `contributor-insight-helper.sh file <compressed_signals.json> <target_slug>`
4. Helper filters for framework-relevant signals (instruction candidates >= 0.65 confidence, error patterns >= 20 occurrences + 2 models)
5. Privacy sanitizes all content before filing
6. Deduplicates against existing open `contributor-insight` issues
7. Files up to 3 issues per run, tagged `contributor-insight`

title: t2148: detect + auto-recover stampless origin:interactive claims
body:
## Summary

Closes the pulse-dispatch-block leak where `origin:interactive` + owner-assigned issues with **no matching stamp** block pulse dispatch forever. Discovered this session while investigating why #19346 and #19347 sat unworked despite the pulse running — the guard treated the label alone as an active claim, but `scan-stale` Phase 1 couldn't see them because no stamp was ever written.

## Evidence

From this session's investigation (before fix):

```
[dispatch_with_dedup] Dedup guard blocked #19346 in marcusquinn/aidevops
[dispatch_with_dedup] Dedup guard blocked #19347 in marcusquinn/aidevops
```

`scan-stale` reported 9 stale claims — none of them #19346/#19347 because no stamp files existed. Memory already logged the workaround: `gh issue edit N --remove-assignee marcusquinn`.

## Root cause

- `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh:513-522` — `_has_active_claim()` returns `true` on `origin:interactive` regardless of stamp state.
- `interactive-session-helper.sh:700-768` — `_isc_cmd_scan_stale()` only iterates `$CLAIM_STAMP_DIR`; stampless claims are invisible.
- `pulse-issue-reconcile.sh:265-312` — `_normalize_unassign_stale()` scopes to `status:queued/in-progress`; bare `origin:interactive + assignee` is out of scope.
- `claim-task-id.sh` auto-assigns runner for `origin:interactive` issues (t1970) without writing a stamp → the leak.

## Fix (two-path, both required)

1. **Discovery (`scan-stale` Phase 1a).** New `_isc_list_stampless_interactive_claims(runner_user, slug)` primitive emits compact JSON lines per match. `_isc_cmd_scan_stale` iterates pulse-enabled repos, surfaces each stampless claim with release command. Does **not** auto-release — it's the interactive session's session-start hook.
2. **Autonomous recovery (`pulse-issue-reconcile.sh`).** New `_normalize_unassign_stampless_interactive` is called from `normalize_active_issue_assignments` as Pass 2b. 24h default threshold, env-overridable via `STAMPLESS_INTERACTIVE_AGE_THRESHOLD`. Unassigns runner, leaves `origin:interactive` label intact (historical fact, not a live claim signal once the assignee is gone).

## Files

- `EDIT .agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper.sh` — new primitive + Phase 1a + docstring update
- `EDIT .agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh` — new helper + coordinator wiring
- `EDIT .agents/scripts/tests/test-interactive-session-claim.sh` — 3 new tests (primitive +/−, Phase 1a integration); stub `gh` extended with `issue list`
- `EDIT .agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-reconcile.sh` — 3 new tests (positive unassign, stamp-present skip, age-threshold guard)
- `EDIT .agents/AGENTS.md` — one-line Phase 1a note under "Interactive issue ownership"
- `EDIT TODO.md` + `NEW todo/tasks/t2148-brief.md`

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-interactive-session-claim.sh` → 21/21 pass (14 prior + 3 new explicit + stub-coverage bumps)
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-reconcile.sh` → 7/7 pass (4 prior + 3 new)
- `shellcheck` clean on all edited shell files
- `markdownlint` clean on edited markdown

## Scope guard

No change to the canonical dedup rule (`_has_active_claim` still treats `origin:interactive` as active). This PR adds the cleanup path so the rule's *input state* eventually becomes safe to dispatch — the existing GH#18352 / t1996 semantics are preserved.

Resolves #19380

title: GH#19370: tighten shell-style-guide.md + fix scanner thrash root cause
body:
## Summary

Two-part fix for #19370 and the scanner loop it surfaced.

**Part 1 — tighten `.agents/reference/shell-style-guide.md` (135 → 112 lines):** delete dead tracking data, not externalize. The brief suggested moving the phased roadmap + audit table into t2053, but **t2053 is already closed** (PR #19180). The roadmap describes completed work; the audit table is a dated 2026-04-15 snapshot. Deletion is correct; externalization would have perpetuated stale content. Preserved: GH#18702 incident rationale, Patterns A/B/C, banned-pattern examples, canonical variable table, migration checklist. Reordered banned-before-allowed for primacy.

**Part 2 — fix the regex bug that caused repeated scanner thrash against the same files.**

## The real bug

`_simplification_backfill_extract_file_path()` in `pulse-simplification-state.sh` parsed three simplification title forms with pattern `[^ ,)]+\.(md|sh)`. The character class excluded space, comma, close-paren — but **not open-paren**. Form B titles like:

```
simplification: tighten agent doc shell style guide (.agents/reference/shell-style-guide.md, 135 lines)
```

captured `(.agents/reference/shell-style-guide.md` with a leading paren. Downstream `[[ -f "${repo_path}/${file_path}" ]] && continue` then silently skipped every form-B issue → state never recorded those files → scanner re-flagged them on every pulse cycle.

**Evidence:** `.agents/configs/simplification-state.json` has **0 entries** for `shell-style-guide.md` despite 8+ merged simplification PRs against it. 1150 `.md` + 85 `.sh` entries total across state — 1100+ files affected by this silent skip.

**This explains the thrash:** 8+ simplification-debt issues against `shell-style-guide.md` and 9+ against `pre-dispatch-validators.md` over 2026-04-14 to 2026-04-16, #19370 itself saw 2 stale recoveries + NMR-escalation before auto-approval. The scanner wasn't "wrong" — it was blind to its own prior work.

## The fix

1-char regex change: `[^ ,)]+` → `[^ ,()]+` (add open-paren to the exclusion class). Added extensive docstring with all three title forms documented.

## Verification

**Regression guard:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-simplification-backfill-extract-path.sh` — 8 cases (form A .md/.sh, form B .md ×2, form C .sh, recheck+A, recheck+B, empty). Verified:

- Without fix: 3 failures (all form-B variants return `(.agents/...`).
- With fix: 8/8 pass.

**ShellCheck:** clean on both modified files.

**Self-heal:** backfill runs every pulse cycle on the 50 most-recently-closed issues. With the regex fixed, form-B files heal organically on subsequent cycles — no one-off migration script needed. Form-A and form-C files were already being recorded correctly.

## Files changed

- `.agents/reference/shell-style-guide.md` — 135 → 112 lines, dead sections deleted
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-simplification-state.sh` — regex fix + expanded docstring
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-simplification-backfill-extract-path.sh` — new, 8-case regression test

## Why this matters

The meta-pattern here is worth naming: a silent-skip bug in a dedup layer produces "stuck" issues that look like worker failure but are actually scanner regression. Workers kept being dispatched against the same file, burning tokens, because the "have we already simplified this?" check was lying. The fix is one character; the value is cutting off an entire class of recurring NMR noise.

Resolves #19370
